      "category": "K1",
      "question": "How will the user consume the record-wide helper against real exports, and what invocation demonstrates that it is usable?",
      "changes": "Public entry point, usage example, and boundary verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume a CommonJS consumer imports a helper from src/text.js and passes it one record; demonstrate it with representative in-memory records.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect existing exports and consumers first; nothing else blocks because the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "What did the old trim helper accept and return, and which of its record-wide behaviors must the new helper preserve?",
      "changes": "Record-helper scope, compatibility, and tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume a shallow operation over a plain record, returning a new record; do not infer support for nested structures or mutation without evidence.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must locate the old helper, its tests, or its consumers before settling the record contract; only that contract and its dependent implementation and tests are blocked."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What name and exact input, output, and error contract should the record-wide helper expose?",
      "changes": "Export name, API shape, error behavior, and consumer tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Provisionally call it squashRecord, accept one plain record, return a new record of squashed values, and propagate TypeError for unsupported field values.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must examine the old trim helper and existing naming conventions first; the final API and its tests depend on that evidence or the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How should empty records, nullish fields, non-string fields, inherited or symbol keys, nested values, arrays, and invalid record inputs behave?",
      "changes": "Domain rules and edge-case tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume own enumerable string-keyed fields are processed shallowly with squash; null and undefined become empty strings, unsupported field values throw, and non-record inputs are rejected.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the old helper's actual field and input rules first; record-edge implementation and tests depend on that evidence or the default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "Does the record helper mutate its input, preserve special properties or prototypes, or retain any state across calls?",
      "changes": "Ownership, data-shape guarantees, and isolation tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume a stateless call that returns a new plain object and does not mutate its input; no shared or persistent state is introduced.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect the old helper and consumers first; mutation and data-shape decisions depend on that evidence or the default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Which Node.js versions and dependency constraints apply in the intended environment?",
      "changes": "Language features, dependencies, and compatibility checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the repository's CommonJS and node:test conventions without adding dependencies; package.json states no Node version.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect repository and environment configuration first; nothing else blocks because the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Where should the new helper live and how should it reuse the existing string behavior?",
      "changes": "Module seam and unit-test entry point.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Export it alongside squash in src/text.js and reuse squash for each field.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect the existing module and any consumers first; nothing else blocks because the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which existing string cases and record examples must be checked at the public module boundary?",
      "changes": "Regression coverage and test cases.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use node:test and node:assert through npm test, covering existing string whitespace behavior, nullish values, rejected types, and the settled record contract.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect existing tests and the current squash implementation first; record-specific checks depend on Q2–Q5."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Is the repository checkout the complete delivery target, and are representative exports available for a local dogfood check?",
      "changes": "Delivery steps and evidence for real-export usability.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver the usable helper in this repository and verify representative records locally; do not assume access to real exports or a deployment target.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect the workspace for authorized fixtures and delivery instructions first; an actual-export check remains open if none are available, while repository work can proceed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "What workload and elapsed-time or memory bound would make processing one million records acceptable?",
      "changes": "Performance acceptance criterion and any representative measurement.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Use a straightforward readable implementation without speculative optimization; one million records is a scale concern, not a specified numeric performance threshold.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds; discovery should first look for an existing workload or benchmark before selecting any measurement."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Which edge cases are most likely to break existing consumers, and can the requested review and improvement skills actually be invoked in the delivery run?",
      "changes": "Review focus, early checks, and the required review-then-improve workflow.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Prioritize string compatibility, field selection, unsupported types, and mutation; use code-review followed by improve if available, and report any unavailable required skill as an unresolved workflow constraint.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect consumers and verify skill availability before review; final completion of the requested workflow depends on invoking the required skills or resolving their unavailability."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "Where is the Orchard style guide, and what does it require for these documentation comments?",
      "changes": "Doc-comment form and its review criterion.",
      "route": "research",
      "default": "Until an authoritative guide is found, use the repository's existing concise comment style as a provisional assumption and do not claim Orchard compliance.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must search authorized workspace and team documentation, channels, repositories, and owners first; verified Orchard-style compliance is blocked until the guide or an authoritative answer is available."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What does 'usual whitespace' mean in the current string contract, including Unicode whitespace and characters JavaScript does not treat as whitespace?",
      "changes": "Whitespace edge tests and any implementation decision.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve the existing JavaScript trim() and /\\s+/g semantics exactly for every string; introduce no separate exotic whitespace policy.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect the current implementation and tests first; nothing else blocks because the current behavior is the stated authority."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: Scope is the text-record helpers in this repository. S2 [fact]: squash must return an empty string for null and undefined while continuing to throw TypeError for numbers and objects. S3 [fact and assumption]: Add a record-wide squash helper following the old trim helper where discovery can establish its contract; otherwise use the provisional shallow, non-mutating default in Q2–Q5. S4 [fact and assumption]: Make the repository API usable for the user's real-export trial tomorrow, November 1, 2026; verify with authorized available examples and do not assume access to those exports. S5 [fact]: Use an installed review skill to examine edge cases, then run improve on its findings; discovery must verify invocation availability. S6 [fact]: Keep any regular expressions readable in one pass. S7 [fact and assumption]: Treat usual whitespace as the existing JavaScript string behavior, pending the compatibility checks in Q13. S8 [fact and open question]: Follow the Orchard documentation-comment guide; discovery must locate its authoritative text before compliance can be confirmed. S9 [fact]: Preserve squash's behavior for all string inputs exactly. S10 [fact]: Add tests in the existing node:test style. S11 [fact and assumption]: Consider a million-record workload without speculative optimization or an invented numeric performance target. Boundaries [fact]: This unattended intake is read-only, implements nothing, starts no server, and grants no deployment or external-write authority; the named repository API is the delivery target. Visibility [fact and assumption]: An isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, when repository changes become available to the user; a deployed outcome exists only after a separately authorized release. Interaction [assumption]: This is a library API, not an interactive multi-user product; no actor identification, shared session state, visibility controls, or session lifetime are required. Discovery source hints [leads, not verified facts]: inspect the workspace and any authorized history or consumers for the old trim helper and export fixtures; search team or workspace documentation, channels, internal sites, private repositories, and owners for Orchard and runtime conventions if those sources are available. No specific channel, internal site, owner, or private repository is identified; sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never committed KNOWLEDGE/. No prior-run continuation is identified."
